ask.text:
The children are out. She has a bundle of cloth on the table, folded twice and tied with cord.

"Three more pairs of hands and no flax to spin. I need a buyer who will not cheat me on the weight, and I cannot go to the yard myself without someone deciding I am for sale."

She says the last part plainly, as a fact about the yard and not about herself.

choices.text: I will take it to the yard and sell it at what it is worth.
I can lend you the silver instead.
choices.unavailableNote: You do not have fifteen shekels to lend, and she would know if you offered less.

choices.text: I have my own affairs to think of.

thanks.text: "Then you are owed." She ties the cord tighter and does not look up. "I will not forget it, and I will not mention it again."

refused.text: "No. Of course not." She cuts the cord with her thumbnail and starts folding the cloth back into the chest, and the room is very quiet.
